questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How supermarkets buy and sell wild food
The dangers of eating poisonous plants
Foraging and the health benefits of wild food
How to grow your own vegetables in the garden
questions.why: They discuss foraging and a new UK project on the health benefits of wild food.

questions.q: When did foraging become popular again?
options: Since the Covid pandemic
In the 1950s
After supermarkets closed
Only in the last month
questions.why: Neil says since the Covid pandemic, foraging has become popular again.

questions.q: What is the Wild Biome Project?
options: A book about a year of eating only wild food
A group that sells wild food online
A course that teaches people to cook mushrooms
A three-month study of wild food and health
questions.why: It is a three-month experiment into the health benefits of adding wild food to your diet.

questions.q: What does forager Rob Gould say about eating wild food?
options: Everyone should eat nothing but wild food
A little gives you many more nutrients
It is too expensive for most families
It has fewer vitamins than shop food
questions.why: He says just including a small amount greatly increases the nutrients and vitamins you get.

questions.q: How does Mo Wilde answer people who say there wouldn't be enough wild food?
options: She says we should import more food
She agrees that foraging should be limited
She says there is never a shortage of nettles
She says only experts should forage
questions.why: She says, 'I've never noticed a shortage of nettles'.

questions.q: Why does Mo Wilde say we might fly nettles in if they didn't grow here?
options: To show how nutritious and valuable they are
Because they taste better from abroad
Because they are hard to find in the UK
To show that they are very expensive
questions.why: She says we'd fly them in as a superfood because they're so nutritious.

questions.q: Which of these do the foragers report?
options: They lost interest in food and ate less
They felt more anxious and stressed
They missed their usual supermarket food
They enjoyed their food's smell and taste more
questions.why: They report greater appreciation for the smell and taste of their food and more self-worth.

questions.q: How did one forager's feelings change during the project?
options: She felt great at first, then tired
She felt low at first, but later much better
She felt ill and left the project
She felt the same all the time
questions.why: She felt 'quite flat' in the first week, but now feels loads better and doesn't want it to stop.
